# Scheuermann juvenile kyphosis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Surgery > Trauma and orthopedic surgery > Spine > Scheuermann juvenile kyphosis*

[Original Article Link](/library/jQ0_Df)

---

## Summary

Scheuermann <u>kyphosis</u> is a growth-related disorder of the <u>thoracic spine</u> that leads to <u>hyperkyphosis</u>. The condition is typically diagnosed in early <u>adolescence</u> following a referral to the physician because of poor posture or a spinal deformity discovered in a school screening program. <u>Subacute back pain</u> is present in some cases. Conventional <u>lateral</u> <u>spine</u> <u>x-rays</u> showing > 40° of <u>kyphosis</u> (normal: 20–40°) and <u>anterior</u> <u>vertebral</u> wedging of > 5° of three or more adjacent <u>vertebrae</u> confirm the diagnosis. First-line therapy includes <u>physical therapy</u> and <u>NSAIDs</u> for <u>pain</u>. Bracing is used for patients with <u>kyphosis</u> greater than 60°, while those with <u>kyphosis</u> greater than 75° or neurological deficits may have to undergo <u>spinal fusion</u> to relieve symptoms. Although symptoms typically resolve when patients reach skeletal maturity, there may be complications such as <u>chronic pain</u>, permanent deformity, <u>degenerative disc disease</u>, <u>spondylolysis</u>, and <u>spondylolisthesis</u> in adulthood.
